newsitem.title: USA: Cool week, wet weekend likely for U.S. Midwest-WSC.
newsitem.headline: Cool week, wet weekend likely for U.S. Midwest-WSC.

text.p: Temperatures should remain below normal on Tuesday and Wednesday in the eastern U.S. Midwest with weekend showers likely, Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio said.

"It starts off cool with below normal temperatures today," Burgio said. "It will be a little warmer tomorrow but still a normal to below normal trend. By Friday, we'll see a better chance of some scattered afternoon showers for the northwest portion of the belt."
Those showers were expected to push eastward across the Mississippi River into the eastern Corn Belt on Sunday or Monday, bringing 0.25 to 1.00 inch with 40 to 60 percent coverage, he said.
"After that, there really isn't much (precipitation) there," Burgio said.

Burgio said long-range models did not suggest a shift to a wetter weather pattern next week. Some forecasters had predicted on Monday that a ridge of high pressure would move west, increasing the likelihood of showers in dry portions of the central Corn Belt.
